notes.text: Implemented the persisted optional counting semaphore across the shared ControlService used by HTTP and MCP. The dashboard can enable a limit from 1 to 64 and shows usage and holders; service status and the MCP get_server_capacity tool expose the same state. Starts acquire atomically, switches retain their slot, failures release it, and lowering the limit preserves running servers. Focused tests cover contention for the final slot, capacity exhaustion, switch retention, failed-start release, persistence, HTTP, MCP, and localization. Keep the item open until the rebuilt controller is explicitly installed and exercised with real managed processes; the active service was not restarted implicitly.

title: Validate the implemented server capacity with owned process cleanup
validation: With capacity two, start two projects and verify a third HTTP start or MCP claim/start cannot spawn a process. Report any retained agent claim separately from the runtime capacity rejection.
Verify two simultaneous requests for the last slot cannot both start, including requests arriving through HTTP and MCP.

Verify switching a running project retains its slot. A failed start releases that slot exactly once only after owned cleanup is confirmed; unconfirmed cleanup continues to occupy capacity and blocks a competing start.
Verify lowering capacity never terminates current processes and status consistently identifies every slot holder.

At stable barriers, full capacity, compact project status and runtime-operation results agree after unconfirmed cleanup and after successful recovery; persisted capacity settings survive an isolated controller restart.

Verify the real dashboard capacity flow: configure limit two, fill it, observe a blocked third start, free and reuse a slot, then lower the limit without terminating either survivor. Keep this separate from fixture-API UI tests.

Record C1-C7 integration outcomes, compact/full regression before and after, browser result and final owned-process cleanup on the tested commit. Cleanup failures fail verification and remain in the report.
